statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and twenty-one of the twenty-four hours published here contain no tradable interval at all; only the three slots from the scheduled 22:00Z Sunday reopen onward are tradable, and they carry conditional Tail readings of 12, 13 and 12 that stay far below the block threshold. Stress is 37, moderate: a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods is live after the collapse of trade talks, Canada has dated a dollar-for-dollar match to 8 September, the 20 August H.15 column shows 4.19% at two years, 4.69% at ten and 5.23% at thirty with the long end at its highest since 2007, and Brent at $94.39 with WTI at $87.06 completes a second consecutive weekly energy gain against an unresolved US-Iran standoff. Confidence is 87, high: Friday's closing levels were cross-checked against two independent sources, and yields, energy prices, volatility and the seven-day calendar are all verified; the only material gap is the absence of a live price path, which is a property of the closed venue rather than of the evidence.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day and below its own open, ending a five-day losing streak, while the VIX settled at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Friday internals were split rather than aligned, with software firm, semiconductors net lower and megacaps five to three higher on roughly 1.8 points of dispersion. Because the venue is shut for twenty-one of the twenty-four hours published here, the first Tail-relevant evidence can only come from prints after the 22:00Z Sunday reopen: whether an opening gap is retraced, whether early pullbacks are meaningful, and whether the tariff, rates and energy channels reprice in an orderly two-way auction. The published danger window is deliberately narrow and covers only those three reopen hours, and the mapped policy state stays green across the whole horizon.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with all three reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through twenty-one shut hours, then carries conditional readings of 12, 13 and 12 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen, while live US tariffs on Canadian goods, a post-2007 long end and a second week of energy gains stay unpriced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T01:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T00:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the first two hours after it all sit inside the horizon. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33%, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session, the close finished below the open, and the day ended a five-day losing streak. That close was cross-checked against two independent public sources this hour after one quote page returned an inconsistent level with its own delayed-data warning. On policy, the 50% US tariff on Canadian goods is in force after trade talks collapsed, and Prime Minister Carney has said Canada will match it dollar for dollar from 8 September across steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, with negotiations suspended and Canadian negotiators recalled. On rates, the 20 August H.15 column shows 4.19% at two years, 4.69% at ten and 5.23% at thirty, with the long end at its highest since 2007 and last week's equity weakness driven by that bond move rather than by index-level structure. On energy, WTI ended the week at $87.06 and Brent at $94.39 after a second consecutive weekly gain, with the Strait of Hormuz still effectively closed; the 60-day US-Iran memorandum lapsed on 17 August, so no new deadline falls inside this horizon. Delayed cross-asset context for the last session shows dispersed rather than aligned internals: software firm, semiconductors net lower with Nvidia, Arm and Intel down, and five of eight megacaps higher on roughly 1.8 points of dispersion. That dispersion is a conflict signal and argues against a Tail amplifier. The week ahead is front-loaded with scheduled checkpoints rather than current risk: 2-year, 5-year and 7-year note auctions Tuesday through Thursday, July PCE and Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 results on Wednesday, and the Jackson Hole symposium opening Thursday with the Warsh keynote at 14:00Z Friday. None of those events falls inside this horizon, so they raise Stress and shape Confidence without lifting current Tail.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is nearly complete: 21 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z, 06:00Z, 21:00Z clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress traced a shallow arc: 35 at the start of the window, a rebuild to 42 through the middle of Saturday as the tariff deadline passed and the Canadian response was dated, then an easing to 38 by the final hour. Confidence stayed in an 85-88 band, reflecting verified closing levels and macro data against the absence of any live price path. Nothing in the window contains observed one-way structure, because no venue was open to produce it.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The following twenty slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them. The last three slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12, the first full hour after it a conditional 13, and the hour coinciding with the Monday Asian cash open a conditional 12, all still green and all resting on gap and thin-liquidity scenarios rather than on observed structure. They are the only reason a narrow danger window is published. Stress eases from 37 to a 35 trough through the Sunday overnight hours, rebuilds steadily to 46 in the final closed hour, peaks at 52 in the reopen slot as the weekend information set converges on a single opening auction, then eases to 50 and 48 as that auction clears. Confidence decays from 87 to 73 across the horizon as verified Friday evidence ages without any live path to refresh it.
